answer.rationale: The release cannot be rolled back (compliance constraint eliminates rollback_release). Regional failover (memory_b2) addresses latency from regional degradation, not write-path saturation under heavy settlement traffic. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) applies to external partner outages, not internal write-path load. Adding capacity could help but carries longer lead time and less direct evidence for this specific symptom pattern. Routing read traffic to read replicas (memory_b5) is the best single intervention: it offloads all non-essential read load from the primary, freeing write capacity during settlement peak while preserving the mandatory security patch. memory_b5 documents that this exact pattern—rerouting report/dashboard queries to read replicas—recovered transactional write latency the same day with no data loss. This keeps customer writes intact, maintains the compliance-mandated release, and can be applied quickly within the single-intervention budget.
